cells.reason: The anchor is a drinking-water MCL (0.010 mg/L for 'community and nontransient-noncommunity public water systems', effective 2024-10-01) and the regulation page itself states it 'is a drinking-water standard, not a food limit' that 'should not be compared directly to a food-occurrence concentration'; carrying 10 µg/L onto a dried as-sold seaweed content cell crosses basis families, which condition (b) forbids, so the 10 derived at face value is not an applicable number. The register holds no food-content Cr-VI row for any food (its 19 Cr-VI rows are drinking water, EN 71-3 toy migration, textiles, leather, RoHS homogeneous materials, tattoo inks and fertilisers), so no same-basis sovereign instrument exists to read across from. The same-basis treatment available is species-bounded-by-parent (Cr-VI at or below the Cr-total cell, currently 2000) or a disclosed baseline screen, not the water MCL.
